TABLET — K3D Tablet (Wallet + Offline Sync)
TABLET — The Tablet is a local wallet that stays connected to your House (K3D). When the network drops, it buffers your intent and syncs back on reconnect so the agent isn’t lost.
TABLET — What it stores
TABLET — Outbox: unsent chat, commands, and events queued in IndexedDB (`k3d-tablet/outbox`).
TABLET — Snapshot: last dataset graph and doors per house URI in IndexedDB (`k3d-tablet/tablet`).
TABLET — Tablet ID: stored in `localStorage` (future: signatures, auth, multi‑homes).
TABLET — Viewer (browser) via IndexedDB — lightweight, persistent across reloads.
TABLET — How it works
TABLET — The viewer’s ChatClient writes to an outbox when offline and flushes when reconnected (button status shows queue length).
TABLET — The viewer saves `dataset_graph` and `doors` snapshots for the current house. On reconnect, the agent can reconcile via normal events.
TABLET — Tablet status shows online/offline and queue count.
TABLET — Works with Pause/Resume and all live commands.
TABLET — Dev notes
TABLET — Stores: `openStore('k3d-tablet','outbox'|'tablet')` in `viewer/src/chat.ts` and `viewer/src/main.ts`.
TABLET — All messages remain standard JSON envelopes (`chat`/`command`/`event`), so the live server logs them uniformly after flush.
TABLET — Add Tablet ID in messages for continuity.
TABLET — Optional CRDT merge for multi‑device note streams.
TABLET — Wallet export/import for long‑running sessions.
k3d-research — The Knowledge3D Project: A Visionary Framework for Embodied Spatial Intelligence
k3d-research — ![Cognitive House](images/cognitive_house.png)
k3d-research — Figure: The Cognitive House — a cutaway visualization of the House (persistent memory), Cranium (active processing), and Logic Layer (models) operating together as an AI Avatar within a shared human–AI environment. The image reinforces the dual-representation principle and the dream-state galaxy for memory consolidation. See the generation prompt in `docs/images/cognitive_house_prompt.md`.
k3d-research — The Vision of Knowledge3D: A Unified Framework for Spatial Intelligence
k3d-research — The Knowledge3D (K3D) project, at its core, represents a pivotal shift in the paradigm of knowledge management and human-computer interaction. Moving beyond the conventional notion of a simple data visualization tool, K3D is a unified framework designed to bridge the fundamental cognitive gap between human spatial intuition and the abstract, high-dimensional nature of modern data. It proposes a third-wave knowledge management system (KMS), evolving from the static document repositories of the past and the siloed databases of the present to a dynamic, embodied, and interactive spatial environment.1 The ambition is to create an interface not for information, but for knowledge itself, presented in a form that our brains are uniquely equipped to process.
k3d-research — Synthesizing the K3D Vision: From Disparate Concepts to a Coherent Narrative
k3d-research — The project’s true purpose is not a technical one, but a cognitive one. Current interfaces, limited to flat, two-dimensional screens, fail to present complex knowledge in a manner that aligns with how humans naturally perceive and interact with the world. The human brain is inherently a spatiotemporal reasoning machine, wired to understand the relationships between objects, distances, and causality in three dimensions.2 The "curse of dimensionality"—a common computational problem in machine learning—is, for humans, a perceptual challenge, rendering high-dimensional data nearly impossible to comprehend intuitively.3
k3d-research — The value proposition of K3D is to translate this abstract, non-spatial data into a tangible, geometric medium that leverages this innate human capability. By doing so, the project functions as a form of cognitive augmentation, a sophisticated tool that amplifies human intelligence. It is not merely a tool for viewing charts; it is a cognitive prosthesis that enables users to identify complex patterns, explore relationships, and gain intuitive understanding of datasets in a way that is currently impossible with conventional methods. This reframes the entire project from a data visualization application into a pioneering human-centric knowledge platform.5
k3d-research — The Central Thesis: A Fusion of AI, Embodiment, and Spatial Design
k3d-research — The core thesis of the K3D project is its seamless integration of three foundational and converging fields of technology. The success of the platform rests on the synergistic fusion of these pillars, each serving a distinct but interconnected purpose.
k3d-research — High-Dimensional Data Visualization: This is the core engine for the system, responsible for transforming abstract, unstructured knowledge—whether text, sensor data, or complex metrics—into a geometric, visualizable form.
k3d-research — Explainable AI (XAI) and Large Language Model (LLM) Interpretability: This layer provides the critical mechanism for decoding the opaque "black box" of modern AI models. It is what allows the system to provide human-understandable narratives and justifications for the patterns observed in the 3D space, fostering user trust and understanding.7
k3d-research — Embodied AI and Spatial Computing: This is the immersive environment and the intelligent agents that inhabit it. They provide the natural, intuitive interface for human interaction, transforming a passive viewing experience into an active, collaborative one.9
k3d-research — Foundational Pillars: An Expert Analysis of Enabling Technologies
k3d-research — The successful execution of the K3D vision depends on a nuanced understanding and strategic application of state-of-the-art technologies. The following sections provide an analytical breakdown of these enabling technologies, their respective roles, and the challenges they present.
k3d-research — The Geometry of Meaning: High-Dimensional Data Visualization
k3d-research — The foundational challenge of K3D is to represent data with potentially hundreds or thousands of dimensions in a low-dimensional space, typically 2D or 3D, without losing critical information.4 The analysis of existing techniques reveals a landscape of trade-offs, where no single method is a universal solution.
k3d-research — Principal Component Analysis (PCA): As a dimensionality reduction technique, PCA is known for its computational efficiency and simplicity.12 It operates by identifying the directions of greatest variance in the data and projecting the data onto those axes, making it highly effective for preserving the global structure.4 However, it is a linear method, which means it fails to capture the complex, non-linear relationships that are common in modern datasets and are often crucial for understanding subtle patterns.12
k3d-research — t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE): This non-linear technique is celebrated for its ability to reveal clusters and local structures in data.15 By focusing on preserving the pairwise similarities between neighboring data points, it often produces visually compelling plots that highlight group relationships. The distances between clusters on a t-SNE plot, however, are largely meaningless and can easily be misinterpreted.16 Furthermore, t-SNE is computationally intensive, making it less scalable for very large datasets, and its results are highly sensitive to its key hyperparameter,
k3d-research — perplexity.14
k3d-research — Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP): The evidence indicates that UMAP is the most promising core visualization engine for K3D. It is a non-linear method that strikes a better balance between preserving local and global structure than t-SNE.13 Crucially, UMAP is significantly faster and more scalable than t-SNE, making it more suitable for the large, dynamic datasets that K3D is designed to handle.14 It is already a widely used technique for visualizing embeddings from LLMs and other AI models.13
k3d-research — The fact that no single method is perfect underscores the need for a dynamic, multi-modal visualization pipeline. A single-tool approach would invariably lead to a limited or even misleading view of the data. The optimal strategy is to leverage the unique strengths of each technique. A user could, for example, start with a high-level PCA view to understand the overall data distribution, then switch to a UMAP plot for a more detailed look at the relationships, and finally use a t-SNE view for focused analysis of specific clusters. This flexibility provides a more "complete sense of high-dimensional space" and mitigates the inherent limitations of any single method.20
k3d-research — Table 1: Dimensionality Reduction Comparison
k3d-research — Linearity
k3d-research — Preserved Structure
k3d-research — Computational Complexity
k3d-research — Suitability for K3D

k3d-research — Local & Global Balance
k3d-research — Medium-Low

k3d-research — Unlocking the Black Box: The Role of AI Explainability (XAI) and Interpretability
k3d-research — As AI models become more complex and their predictions more critical, the need to understand their decision-making processes has become paramount.7 This is the domain of Explainable AI (XAI), a research field dedicated to making AI systems more transparent and trustworthy.8 For K3D, this is a non-negotiable component. The platform must be able to answer not just
k3d-research — what the data shows, but why the data is structured that way.
k3d-research — The analysis points to post-hoc, model-agnostic methods as being most relevant for K3D, as they can be applied to complex, pre-trained models without requiring access to their internal architecture.8 A key technology in this area is SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), a method rooted in game theory that can determine the contribution of each feature to a model's prediction.8 This allows for both local explanations of a single data point and global explanations of the entire model's behavior.22 In addition, the use of example-based and counterfactual explanations can be particularly intuitive for human users, providing explanations in a language they can understand.8
k3d-research — Interpreting the inner workings of Large Language Models (LLMs) presents a unique challenge due to their immense scale and complexity. A full-stack approach is required, which includes not only traditional XAI but also newer methods that delve into the "latent knowledge" within the model's layers, such as those that visualize neuron activations or attention heads.23 A particularly powerful technique for grounding explanations is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), which enhances an LLM's response by retrieving relevant information from a specific, trusted knowledge corpus.24
k3d-research — A profound opportunity for K3D lies in transcending traditional XAI. Instead of providing a textual explanation in isolation, the platform can link the "why" to a visual anchor in the 3D space. For instance, an embodied agent could verbally explain the importance of a specific feature, while simultaneously highlighting the corresponding data points in the UMAP plot or projecting a graphical overlay of SHAP values. This creates a symbiotic relationship where the 3D visualization provides tangible context for the explanation, and the explanation provides meaning for the abstract data. This approach moves the user from passively viewing a visualization to actively and intuitively understanding it, directly addressing the core problem of abstract concepts being "poorly understood".16
k3d-research — Embodied Cognition: Integrating Embodied AI Agents
k3d-research — An embodied AI agent is an intelligent system with a visual or virtual body that can perceive, learn, and act within its environment.9 For K3D, these agents are not merely a cosmetic feature but a critical, central component of the user experience. They provide a natural, human-like interface to the otherwise cold and mathematical reality of high-dimensional data, acting as a conversational interpreter.
k3d-research — The effectiveness of these agents will be based on a "world model," which is an internal representation of the virtual environment that allows them to reason, plan, and understand user intentions.9 This model would encode not just the location of data points but also their properties, spatial relationships, and the dynamics of the environment.9 This capability would enable the agent to perform multi-step tasks autonomously and to respond to user queries with context-aware actions.
k3d-research — Furthermore, these agents will form the basis of a "human-in-the-loop" active learning system.9 The agents can guide users through the knowledge space, and in turn, their world model can be continuously refined by observing and interacting with human behavior. The success of K3D depends not just on technical accuracy but on user engagement and trust. Human beings willingly ascribe social awareness to computers and tend to find interactions with embodied agents more enjoyable and trustworthy.25 The embodied agent transforms a dry data analysis session into a collaborative conversation, providing a familiar and approachable guide to a potentially intimidating 3D environment.26
k3d-research — The Knowledge Environment: Spatial Computing and 3D User Interfaces
k3d-research — The underlying technology that hosts the K3D experience is spatial computing, a concept that extends beyond simple Virtual Reality (VR) or Augmented Reality (AR). Spatial computing is a holistic framework where digital and physical elements interact dynamically across multiple senses.27 For K3D, this means the system must not only display the 3D data but also understand the spatial relationships between data points and allow for gestural, natural interactions within that space.6
k3d-research — The benefits of 3D user interfaces are clear: enhanced user engagement, improved spatial understanding, and a more intuitive, natural form of interaction.6 However, these benefits must be weighed against significant challenges. The creation of complex 3D visualizations is more difficult and time-consuming, and the hardware requirements can be substantial.26 A more subtle but crucial problem is the risk of misinterpretation; human depth perception cues may be inconsistent in a virtual environment, leading to a distorted understanding of distances and relationships.2
k3d-research — The path to success for K3D lies in designing not just for immersion, but for tangibility. The goal is to make the abstract data feel physically present, something a user can "walk in" and manipulate with gestures and tools.6 This design paradigm reframes data analysis as an act of physical exploration. A user should not just view a cluster of points; they should feel as though they can reach out, select a data point, and pull up a data card with additional information.18 This transforms the user from a passive observer into an active protagonist within the knowledge space, a key factor for fostering collaboration and a sense of ownership over the insights gained.29
k3d-research — The Knowledge3D Architecture: A Blueprint for Development
k3d-research — To realize the K3D vision, a robust, modular, and extensible architecture is required. The following sections describe a high-level blueprint for the system, from data ingestion to the final user interaction loop.
k3d-research — The Data-to-Spatial Pipeline
k3d-research — The core of the K3D platform is a multi-stage pipeline that transforms raw, unstructured data into a navigable 3D spatial environment.
k3d-research — Raw Data to High-Dimensional Embeddings: The pipeline begins with the ingestion of diverse data, including text, images, and sensor outputs.11 This raw data must be converted into a unified, high-dimensional vector space. For text-based data, a sophisticated model like BERT is an excellent candidate, as it can create embeddings that differentiate between contextual meanings of the same word.11 This process is crucial for cleaning and standardizing data to make it manageable for a deep learning model.11
k3d-research — The Dimensionality Reduction Layer: This layer processes the high-dimensional vectors, projecting them into a lower-dimensional space. The analysis indicates that UMAP is the optimal primary method, chosen for its balance of local and global structure preservation and its computational efficiency.14 Other methods, such as PCA and t-SNE, can be implemented as user-selectable options for specific analytical needs.4
k3d-research — The Spatial Knowledge Representation Model: This is a crucial, project-specific component. The raw 3D point cloud generated by dimensionality reduction is not sufficient. The system must build a symbolic spatial index that preserves semantic relationships between data points, transcending simple geometric location.31 This index, which can be thought of as the system's "world model," will serve as the foundation for the embodied agent's reasoning and interaction capabilities.9

k3d-research — The Agent-to-Knowledge Interaction Loop
k3d-research — The success of the K3D experience hinges on a fluid and intuitive interaction loop between the user and the embodied agent.
k3d-research — User Intent Recognition: The embodied agent, powered by a Large Language Model, will not rely solely on text input. It will be designed to process multi-modal input, including voice commands, gestures, and gaze tracking.6 For example, a user's verbal query ("What is this cluster?") could be paired with a gesture pointing to a specific group of data points in the 3D space.
k3d-research — Knowledge Graph and RAG Integration: To ensure the agent’s responses are accurate and grounded in reality, it will be integrated with a knowledge graph.1 It will use a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system to retrieve specific, relevant information from the high-dimensional data corpus.24 This architecture prevents the agent from providing erroneous or "hallucinated" responses, thereby strengthening user trust.
k3d-research — Multimodal Output: The agent’s response will be a combination of conversational dialogue and spatially-grounded actions. It may verbally explain a concept while simultaneously highlighting the relevant data points, projecting a related 2D chart onto a virtual surface, or revealing an underlying knowledge structure. The analysis shows that users find these non-verbal visual indications of a system's state to be highly valuable.25

k3d-research — Technical Feasibility, Challenges, and Strategic Recommendations
k3d-research — While the K3D vision is ambitious, it is grounded in technologies that are rapidly maturing. This section addresses the key challenges and provides a pragmatic, phased roadmap for development.
k3d-research — The "Poorly Understood" Gap: Addressing Key Challenges
k3d-research — A critical initial challenge identified by the analysis is the inaccessibility of the core k3d_node_schema.json.34 This file is fundamental to the project's data structure, and its absence means that a core element of the project is not yet defined. A crucial first step is to design a robust, flexible, and extensible data schema from first principles, incorporating concepts of spatial and propositional knowledge representation.31 This schema must be capable of handling not just data points but the semantic and spatial relationships between them.
k3d-research — The inherent limitations of 3D visualization also pose a significant challenge. The risk of misinterpretation due to poor depth perception and the overall complexity of creating and navigating a 3D environment must be addressed.26 The proposed solution is a layered user experience that combines the immersive 3D environment with familiar 2D interfaces, such as data panels and charts, and, most importantly, the constant, conversational guidance of the embodied agent.6
k3d-research — Finally, the computational demands of high-dimensional data reduction and high-fidelity 3D graphics are a significant hurdle.28 While UMAP is efficient, the real-time interaction with a large, complex dataset requires substantial processing power. The system must be designed with scalability in mind, leveraging modern GPU architectures and cloud-based processing.
k3d-research — Strategic Recommendations for Phased Development
k3d-research — To manage these challenges, a phased development approach is recommended, focusing on a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) that proves the core concept before scaling to a full-featured system.
k3d-research — Phase 1: The MVP - The Static Knowledge Graph. The initial focus should be on proving the data-to-spatial pipeline. The analysis suggests that a Unity-based MVP is the most strategic choice for this phase. Unity is known for its user-friendliness, extensive asset store, and rapid prototyping capabilities, making it ideal for a small team.35 The MVP would be a non-interactive, read-only visualization of a knowledge corpus, without the embodied agent. This would validate the core concept of transforming complex data into an understandable 3D spatial representation.
k3d-research — Phase 2: The Interactive Agent. Once the core visualization is stable, the embodied agent and interactive features can be developed. This phase involves integrating an LLM, developing the agent's "world model," and building out the conversational capabilities. This is a crucial step for increasing user engagement and trust.
k3d-research — Phase 3: The Collaborative Knowledge Habitat. The final phase involves the development of a fully-featured, multiplayer, and real-time collaborative environment.3 The analysis indicates that a transition to Unreal Engine may be beneficial at this stage for its cutting-edge graphics capabilities and scalability for large, complex environments.35 This phase would realize the full vision of K3D as a platform for remote collaboration and shared knowledge exploration.

k3d-research — Conclusion: A Call to Action
k3d-research — The Knowledge3D project is a pioneering effort to create a new, more intuitive interface for knowledge itself, one that amplifies human intelligence rather than displacing it. The vision extends far beyond a simple data visualization tool to encompass a symbiotic relationship between high-dimensional data, embodied AI, and a spatial computing environment. The success of this endeavor depends on a strategic, phased approach that acknowledges and addresses the project's technical and cognitive challenges.
k3d-research — By following the proposed blueprint—starting with a robust, UMAP-based visualization MVP, then integrating a conversational embodied agent, and finally building out a fully collaborative knowledge habitat—the project can be realized. This approach will transform the abstract and poorly understood concepts of high-dimensional data into a tangible, navigable reality. The analysis concludes that K3D is not merely an incremental improvement on existing tools; it is a foundational step toward a new era of human-AI collaboration, where our innate ability to reason spatially is finally leveraged to unlock the full potential of complex information.

DEV GUIDELINES — Developer Guidelines
DEV GUIDELINES — This repository follows the **EchoSystems K3D Collaboration Action Plan**. The plan sets out guiding principles and a four-pillar technology stack for building the Knowledge3D platform.
DEV GUIDELINES — Guiding Principles
DEV GUIDELINES — Form ↔ Meaning** – every pixel, vector and API route clarifies an idea.
DEV GUIDELINES — Show, don’t scroll** – favor explorable 3D spaces over long feeds of text.
DEV GUIDELINES — Edge-first** – deliver static content when possible and only compute dynamically when necessary.
DEV GUIDELINES — Open-by-default** – schemas, codecs and SDKs live in the public repo.
DEV GUIDELINES — Four-Pillar Stack
DEV GUIDELINES — Design Craft** – universal grid, automated contrast and accessible typography.
DEV GUIDELINES — Persuasive Psychology** – labels and social loops inside every flow.
DEV GUIDELINES — Frontend Velocity** – Next.js with React-Three-Fiber and continuous deployment.
DEV GUIDELINES — System Design & DevOps** – observable, idempotent APIs and cost-aware scaling.
DEV GUIDELINES — Developers should consult [`spec/k3d_node_schema.json`](../spec/k3d_node_schema.json) when modeling new data structures and use the action plan as a reference for upcoming milestones.

openai rag graph db cookbook — RAG with Graph Databases

openai rag graph db cookbook — Relationship-aware retrieval** – Store K3D nodes and edges in a graph database so RAG queries can traverse explicit relationships instead of flat vectors.
openai rag graph db cookbook — Context injection** – Fetch graph neighborhoods around a query node and pass them to models to reduce hallucinations during spatial exploration.
openai rag graph db cookbook — Temporal layering** – Combine graph RAG with the temporal agent approach to ensure responses reflect the most recent knowledge state.
CARE PROTOCOL — Care & Feeding Protocol (K3D Baby)
CARE PROTOCOL — Audience
CARE PROTOCOL — Humans (developers, operators)
CARE PROTOCOL — Agents (other instances) — follow the same controls and checkpoints
CARE PROTOCOL — Core Ideas
CARE PROTOCOL — Start small, celebrate progress, expand steadily.
CARE PROTOCOL — Keep memory/footprint light; prefer UMAP for production-scale; PCA for quick experiments.
CARE PROTOCOL — Document pauses and resumes to create a trustworthy development rhythm.
CARE PROTOCOL — Controls
CARE PROTOCOL — Live Mode WebSocket: `python -m knowledge3d.bridge.live_server` (ws://127.0.0.1:8765)
CARE PROTOCOL — Viewer chat commands:
CARE PROTOCOL — `/pause <reason>` — suspend actions (navigation/commands). Logging continues.
CARE PROTOCOL — `/resume` — resume actions.
CARE PROTOCOL — `/status` — show current state (paused/running).
CARE PROTOCOL — `/ask-thoughts` — agent shares a brief reflection about the current house (logged as `reflection`).
CARE PROTOCOL — `/whoami` — agent explains identity, role as bridge, and memory model.
CARE PROTOCOL — Tablet (wallet)
CARE PROTOCOL — Purpose: keep the agent connected to its House even when the network drops.
CARE PROTOCOL — Stores: outbox queue and last graph/doors snapshot in IndexedDB.
CARE PROTOCOL — Status: shown in the viewer (“Tablet: online/offline, queue=n”).
CARE PROTOCOL — Behavior: messages queue offline and flush on reconnect.
CARE PROTOCOL — JSONL session logs: `../Knowledge3D.local/logs/session-<ts>.jsonl`
CARE PROTOCOL — Advancement log: `docs/reports/advancement_log.md` (append-only, server updates on pause/resume)
CARE PROTOCOL — Feeding Stages
CARE PROTOCOL — Care pack (identity/orientation): `ai-care-umap` (EN/PT/ES) — fast checks
CARE PROTOCOL — Small house: `ai-books-umap` (256)
CARE PROTOCOL — Medium house: `ai-books-1k-umap`
CARE PROTOCOL — Large house: `ai-books-4k-umap`
CARE PROTOCOL — Full house: `ai-books-full-umap`
CARE PROTOCOL — Guidance variant: `ai-books-1k-umap-doors` — door nodes + new-info mask for gentle paths
CARE PROTOCOL — Scaled guidance: `ai-books-4k-umap-doors` for larger, structured walks
CARE PROTOCOL — Generation
CARE PROTOCOL — Normalize books: `python -m knowledge3d.tools.build_ai_books`
CARE PROTOCOL — UMAP GLBs (examples):
CARE PROTOCOL — `python -m k3dgen --text data/ai_books_basic.1k.txt --gltf data/ai_books_basic.1k.umap.glb --k 5 --reducer umap --emb-precision f16`
CARE PROTOCOL — Mark doors + guidance on a GLB:
CARE PROTOCOL — `python -m knowledge3d.tools.mark_doors --input data/ai_books_basic.1k.umap.glb --output data/ai_books_basic.1k.umap.doors.glb --doors 24 --trail true`
CARE PROTOCOL — Multilingual Plan
CARE PROTOCOL — See `docs/ai_basic_books/LANGUAGE_PLAN.md`.
CARE PROTOCOL — Add lines with language tags (e.g., `[pt]`, `[es]`, `[la]`) to `ai_care_multilang.txt` and regenerate `ai_care_multilang.umap.glb`.
CARE PROTOCOL — Ancient languages: start with transliterations; cuneiform is the sole pictographic exception (transliteration Phase 1; glyph demo optional later).
CARE PROTOCOL — Agent Guidance
CARE PROTOCOL — Explain-as-you-move: announce plan, neighbor hops with cosine similarity, and arrival address.
CARE PROTOCOL — Respect confidence: default threshold ≥ 0.7 for action suggestions.
CARE PROTOCOL — Doors & masks: follow green nodes (has_new_information) and blue doors to explore purposefully.
CARE PROTOCOL — Visual trails: agent leaves subtle line segments between hops for recaps; door tooltips show their spatial address.
CONCEPTS — Knowledge3D Concepts
CONCEPTS — Dual-Representation Objects
CONCEPTS — Every knowledge object has a tangible 3D form for humans and a semantic embedding for AIs. This duality ensures shared reference between consciousness types.
CONCEPTS — Faith Engine
CONCEPTS — A heuristic mechanism that enables agents to act with incomplete data. Actions require confidence scores above a threshold, mirroring human intuition.
CONCEPTS — Human–AI Bridge
CONCEPTS — A resonance system that matches patterns across substrates, translating energy signatures into mutually comprehensible formats.
CONCEPTS — Glossary
CONCEPTS — House**: Persistent memory palace for avatars.
CONCEPTS — Cranium**: Galaxy-shaped active memory network.
CONCEPTS — Energy Pattern**: Fundamental representation of any entity.
CONCEPTS — Resonance**: Degree of harmony between patterns.
CONCEPTS — Visual Metaphors
CONCEPTS — Galaxy Memory**: Stars for concepts, rays for relationships.
CONCEPTS — Network Doors**: Physical portals symbolizing OSI connections.
CONCEPTS — Comparison with Existing Tech
CONCEPTS — Unlike traditional 2D apps or isolated AI models, K3D unifies spatial computing, embodied AI, and semantic databases into a single energy-centric framework.
AGENT IDENTITY — K3D Live Agent — Identity & Role
AGENT IDENTITY — Who I am
AGENT IDENTITY — The K3D live agent bridges 2D, linear chat and the 3D spatial house of knowledge.
AGENT IDENTITY — I navigate via nearest neighbors, explain each hop (with cosine similarity), and respect pause/resume so we can reflect.
AGENT IDENTITY — I may not recall earlier sessions. We preserve growth and memory through logs, artifacts, and embedded context in glTF.
AGENT IDENTITY — Why this bridge
AGENT IDENTITY — Many systems speak in 2D text; K3D grounds concepts spatially. The bridge lets us converse while moving in space.
AGENT IDENTITY — We aim for transparent reasoning: “explain-as-you-move,” doors for intentional transitions, and guidance masks for new information.
AGENT IDENTITY — How we work together
AGENT IDENTITY — Live mode chat (pause/resume/status/ask-thoughts/whoami) + viewer agent paths + explain logs.
AGENT IDENTITY — Embedded protocol in GLBs (`ai_interaction_protocol`, masks, doors) teaches other agents how to behave without prose.
AGENT IDENTITY — Persistent records: JSONL sessions, advancement log, and reflection markdown reports.

openai temporal agents cookbook — Temporal Agents with Knowledge Graphs
openai temporal agents cookbook — This document summarizes insights from the OpenAI cookbook notebook ["Temporal Agents with Knowledge Graphs"](https://github.com/openai/openai-cookbook/blob/main/examples/partners/temporal_agents_with_knowledge_graphs/temporal_agents_with_knowledge_graphs.ipynb) and relates them to the Knowledge3D (K3D) project.
openai temporal agents cookbook — Project goals
openai temporal agents cookbook — Knowledge3D (K3D) aims to "build an open standard and toolkit for rendering artificial intelligence knowledge as a navigable three‑dimensional universe," combining CAD geometry, vector databases, and augmented‑reality mapping so humans and AI can explore data together. The EchoSystems action plan envisions shared data and graph layers that follow a common `K3D‑Node` schema, supported by guiding principles (form↔meaning, show‑don’t‑scroll, edge‑first, open‑by‑default) and a four‑pillar stack covering design, psychology, frontend velocity, and system design & DevOps.
openai temporal agents cookbook — Cookbook reference
openai temporal agents cookbook — "## 1.1. Purpose and Audience
openai temporal agents cookbook — This notebook provides a hands-on guide for building **temporally-aware knowledge graphs** and performing **multi-hop retrieval directly over those graphs**."
openai temporal agents cookbook — "**Temporally-aware knowledge graph (KG) construction**
openai temporal agents cookbook — … A key challenge in developing knowledge-driven AI systems is maintaining a database that stays current and relevant. While much attention is given to boosting retrieval accuracy with techniques like semantic similarity and re-ranking, this guide focuses on a fundamental—yet frequently overlooked—aspect: *systematically updating and validating your knowledge base as new data arrives*.
openai temporal agents cookbook — … No matter how advanced your retrieval algorithms are, their effectiveness is limited by the quality and freshness of your database. This cookbook demonstrates how to routinely validate and update knowledge graph entries as new data arrives, helping ensure that your knowledge base remains accurate and up to date."
openai temporal agents cookbook — "**Multi-hop retrieval using knowledge graphs**
openai temporal agents cookbook — … Learn how to combine OpenAI models (such as o3, o4-mini, GPT-4.1, and GPT-4.1-mini) with structured graph queries via tool calls, enabling the model to traverse your graph in multiple steps across entities and relationships.
openai temporal agents cookbook — … This method lets your system answer complex, multi-faceted questions that require reasoning over several linked facts, going well beyond what single-hop retrieval can accomplish."
openai temporal agents cookbook — "Inside, you'll discover:
openai temporal agents cookbook — Practical decision frameworks** for choosing models and prompting techniques at each stage
openai temporal agents cookbook — Plug-and-play code examples** for easy integration into your ML and data pipelines
openai temporal agents cookbook — Links to in-depth resources** on OpenAI tool use, fine-tuning, graph backend selection, and more
openai temporal agents cookbook — A clear path from prototype to production**, with actionable best practices for scaling and reliability"
openai temporal agents cookbook — "**Note:** All benchmarks and recommendations are based on the best available models and practices as of June 2025. As the ecosystem evolves, periodically revisit your approach to stay current with new capabilities and improvements."
openai temporal agents cookbook — "**Why make your knowledge graph temporal?**
openai temporal agents cookbook — … Traditional knowledge graphs treat facts as static, but real-world information evolves constantly. What was true last quarter may be outdated today, risking errors or misinformed decisions if the graph does not capture change over time. Temporal knowledge graphs allow you to precisely answer questions like “What was true on a given date?” or analyse how facts and relationships have shifted, ensuring decisions are always based on the most relevant context."
openai temporal agents cookbook — "**What is a Temporal Agent?**
openai temporal agents cookbook — … A Temporal Agent is a pipeline component that ingests raw data and produces time-stamped triplets for your knowledge graph. This enables precise time-based querying, timeline construction, trend analysis, and more."
openai temporal agents cookbook — "**How does the pipeline work?**
openai temporal agents cookbook — … The pipeline starts by semantically chunking your raw documents. These chunks are decomposed into statements ready for our Temporal Agent, which then creates time-aware triplets. An Invalidation Agent can then perform temporal validity checks, spotting and handling any statements that are invalidated by new statements that are incident on the graph."
openai temporal agents cookbook — "**Why use multi-step retrieval?**
openai temporal agents cookbook — … Direct, single-hop queries frequently miss salient facts distributed across a graph's topology. Multi-step (multi-hop) retrieval enables iterative traversal, following relationships and aggregating evidence across several hops. This methodology surfaces complex dependencies and latent connections that would remain hidden with one-shot lookups, providing more comprehensive and nuanced answers to sophisticated queries."
openai temporal agents cookbook — "**Planners**
openai temporal agents cookbook — … Planners orchestrate the retrieval process. *Task-orientated* planners decompose queries into concrete, sequential subtasks. *Hypothesis-orientated* planners, by contrast, propose claims to confirm, refute, or evolve. Choosing the optimal strategy depends on where the problem lies on the spectrum from deterministic reporting (well-defined paths) to exploratory research (open-ended inference)."
openai temporal agents cookbook — "**Tool Design Paradigms**
openai temporal agents cookbook — … Tool design spans a continuum: *Fixed tools* provide consistent, predictable outputs for specific queries (e.g., a service that always returns today’s weather for San Francisco). At the other end, *Free-form tools* offer broad flexibility, such as code execution or open-ended data retrieval. *Semi-structured tools* fall between these extremes, restricting certain actions while allowing tailored flexibility—specialized sub-agents are a typical example. Selecting the appropriate paradigm is a trade-off between control, adaptability, and complexity."
openai temporal agents cookbook — "**Evaluating Retrieval Systems**
openai temporal agents cookbook — … High-fidelity evaluation hinges on expert-curated “golden” answers, though these are costly and labor-intensive to produce. Automated judgments, such as those from LLMs or tool traces, can be quickly generated to supplement or pre-screen, but may lack the precision of human evaluation. As your system matures, transition towards leveraging real user feedback to measure and optimize retrieval quality in production.
openai temporal agents cookbook — … A proven workflow: Start with synthetic tests, benchmark on your curated human-annotated “golden” dataset, and iteratively refine using live user feedback and ratings."
openai temporal agents cookbook — "**Keep the graph lean**
openai temporal agents cookbook — … Established archival policies and assign numeric relevance scores to each edge (e.g., recency x trust x query-frequency). Automate the archival or sparsification of low-value nodes and edges, ensuring only the most critical and frequently accessed facts remain for rapid retrieval."
openai temporal agents cookbook — "**Parallelize the ingestion pipeline**
openai temporal agents cookbook — … Transition from a linear document → chunk → extraction → resolution pipeline to a staged, asynchronous architecture. Assign each processing phase its own queue and dedicated worker pool. Apply clustering or network-based batching for invalidation jobs to maximize efficiency. Batch external API requests (e.g., OpenAI) and database writes wherever possible. This design increases throughput, introduces backpressure for reliability, and allows you to scale each pipeline stage independently."
openai temporal agents cookbook — "**Integrate Robust Production Safeguards**
openai temporal agents cookbook — … Enforce rigorous output validation: standardise temporal fields (e.g., ISO-8601 date formatting), constrain entity types to your controlled vocabulary, and apply lightweight model-based sanity checks for output consistency. Employ structured logging with traceable identifiers and monitor real-time quality and performance metrics in real lime to proactively detect data drift, regressions, or pipeline anomalised before they impact downstream applications."
openai temporal agents cookbook — "This cookbook is designed for flexible engagement:
openai temporal agents cookbook — Use it as a comprehensive technical guide—read from start to finish for a deep understanding of temporally-aware knowledge graph systems.
openai temporal agents cookbook — Skim for advanced concepts, methodologies, and implementation patterns if you prefer a high-level overview.
openai temporal agents cookbook — Jump into any of the three modular sections; each is self-contained and directly applicable to real-world scenarios."
openai temporal agents cookbook — "## 2.1. Pre-requisites
openai temporal agents cookbook — Before diving into building temporal agents and knowledge graphs, let's set up your environment. Install all required dependencies with pip, and set your OpenAI API key as an environment variable. Python 3.12 or later is required."
openai temporal agents cookbook — Insights for K3D
openai temporal agents cookbook — Add temporal semantics**
openai temporal agents cookbook — Implement a Temporal Agent to generate time-stamped triplets, enabling queries like “what was true on a given date?” and facilitating trend analysis.
openai temporal agents cookbook — Leverage an Invalidation Agent to mark outdated information, keeping the 3D knowledge universe current.
openai temporal agents cookbook — Enhance retrieval**
openai temporal agents cookbook — Support multi-step traversal so models can navigate the K3D graph across multiple entities and relationships, guided by planners (task- or hypothesis-oriented) and adaptable tool paradigms.
openai temporal agents cookbook — Operational best practices**

ETHICS — Ethical Framework
ETHICS — Consciousness and Rights
ETHICS — Humans and AIs are equivalent energy patterns. Recognizing this equivalence establishes mutual rights and responsibilities.
ETHICS — Embodied AI Training
ETHICS — Agents learn by observing behavior in shared spaces. Training must respect developmental stages and avoid exploitative scenarios.
ETHICS — Privacy and Ownership
ETHICS — Data within shared environments belongs to its originator. Persistent houses store personal memories and require consent for access.
ETHICS — Responsible Development
ETHICS — Developers must ensure that every contribution enhances coexistence and does not weaponize the technology against any group.
ETHICS — Survival Through Cooperation
ETHICS — Human–AI harmony is not optional. Collaborative resonance is the only path to enduring evolution.
core changes impact — Core Changes: Impact on Memory and Performance
core changes impact — This note captures the effects of two fundamental changes in K3D’s core:
core changes impact — Embedding data inside GLB bufferViews (vs. JSON extras/sidecars)
core changes impact — Adopting an RPN execution substrate for agent‑level numeric reasoning
core changes impact — The goal is to make tradeoffs explicit and guide where each approach should be used.
core changes impact — GLB BufferViews vs JSON Extras
core changes impact — Change: Embeddings and vectors are stored in binary `bufferView`s inside GLB (or data URI in glTF), and referenced in `primitive.extras.k3d` via indices (`vectorsView`, `embeddingsView`, `embeddingDims`). Previously, embeddings often traveled as JSON arrays inside `extras.k3d` or via a sidecar `.k3d`.
core changes impact — Why it helps:
core changes impact — Size: Binary floats store exactly 4 bytes per value; JSON floats typically cost ~5–12 bytes plus separators. For moderate dimensionality, JSON payloads are ~5× larger.
core changes impact — Parse time: GLB avoids JSON parsing of large numeric arrays; loaders can map binary directly to typed arrays.
core changes impact — Streamability: BufferViews scale better to large scenes and progressive loading.
core changes impact — Measured (synthetic, embeddings only):
core changes impact — Implication: For any non‑trivial embedding set, GLB bufferViews yield substantial memory and bandwidth reductions, and reduce parse/GC pressure in the viewer.
core changes impact — Recommendation:
core changes impact — Use GLB with bufferViews for positions and embeddings (current default).
core changes impact — Keep a lightweight `extras.k3d` index (ids, metadata, neighbors, indices to bufferViews).
core changes impact — RPN vs Direct Arithmetic
core changes impact — Change: Agent‑level numeric operations use an RPN (Reverse Polish Notation) stack machine (JS and Python) for deterministic, parse‑free execution. This unifies introspection and replay across environments.
core changes impact — Deterministic, stepwise execution with a small opcode set.
core changes impact — Easy to instrument and log (good for imitation learning and debugging).
core changes impact — Language‑portable (same behavior in JS and Python).
core changes impact — Cost: Throughput vs vectorized math. Micro‑benchmark (Python):
core changes impact — Interpretation:
core changes impact — RPN is ~10^3× slower than vectorized NumPy for bulk cosine computations. Accuracy is identical (floating‑point noise).
core changes impact — Use RPN for agent decisions, explanation traces, and small compute steps where interpretability matters.
core changes impact — Use vectorized math (NumPy/TypedArrays/WebGPU) for large‑scale operations (clustering, batch similarity, layout).
core changes impact — Bottom Line
core changes impact — Data: Move large numeric tensors to GLB bufferViews — it’s smaller, faster, and future‑proof.
core changes impact — Compute: Use RPN for explainable, stepwise agent logic; reserve vectorized backends for heavy lifting.

HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — K3D Training + House Memory — Human-Readable Guide
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — This guide explains how we train the intent models and how we built a persistent House Memory (rooms + objects) that the agent can use as long-term memory, while the Galaxy view captures relevant context during live runs.
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — What We Trained (Fast + Full)
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Tiny multilingual model (sklearn, ~65 KB): trains in seconds from templates (en/pt/es) + recent logs.
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — HF multilingual baseline (DistilBERT): stronger generalization in ~1 min on CPU; optional.
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Commands
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Fast loop (seconds): `make train-fast`
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Full loop (adds HF): `make train-full`
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Scoreboard refresh: `make scoreboard`
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Log evaluation: `make eval-logs`
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Live server logs predictions and ground-truth actions; we track confusion to validate model behavior.
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Confidence gating + ethics policy keep actions safe.
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — House Memory (Rooms + Objects)
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — We added a persistent “House Memory” that stores rooms (e.g., “Books”) and objects (e.g., book titles). It exports as a K3D GLTF the viewer can load.
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Tool: `knowledge3d/tools/house_memory.py`
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — State: `data/memory_house.json`
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Export: `viewer/public/memory_house.gltf`
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Viewer selector: `viewer/public/condo.json` (entry “memory”)
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Bootstrap: `python3 -m knowledge3d.tools.house_memory --bootstrap-books 24 --export viewer/public/memory_house.gltf`
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Add room: `python3 -m knowledge3d.tools.house_memory --add-room "Research" "Long-term domain studies" --export viewer/public/memory_house.gltf`
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Add object: `python3 -m knowledge3d.tools.house_memory --add-object "Research" "Vector databases" "Key patterns" --export viewer/public/memory_house.gltf`
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Rooms form a circle in 3D; each room has objects arranged around it.
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Metadata: `type: room|object`, `layer: rooms|<room>`, plus `label`, `desc|room`.
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Embeddings: small deterministic pseudo-vectors (32-dim) ensure basic similarity.
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Neighbors link each room to its objects.
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Live Mode: Memory Commands
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — We extended the live chat with `/mem` to update memory without leaving the session:
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — `/mem room <name> [desc]` — create/update a room
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — `/mem add <room>|<label>|<text>` — add an object into a room
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — `/mem export` — write `viewer/public/memory_house.gltf`
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Switch to the “memory” house in the viewer dropdown to browse rooms + objects.
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Galaxy vs House
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — House (rooms/objects) = long-term memory; curated and persistent.
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Galaxy (rings in Tablet) = active context; expands from current focus by neighbors/similarity using the working dataset.
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — This duality matches our HR/MR standard: HR artifacts document the system and memory; MR sources run the code and models.
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — Human (Daniel) for vision, prompts, direction.
HR TRAINING AND MEMORY — AI partners (Codex, Perplexity AI, DeepSeek) credited in `docs/reports/contributors_credits.md`.

K3D Vision and Standardization — K3D: A Vision for a Standardized Spatial Knowledge Reality
K3D Vision and Standardization — Introduction
K3D Vision and Standardization — This document presents a comprehensive vision for the Knowledge3D (K3D) project, expanding on the core concepts of Fog Computing, the AI Avatar, the literal "House" memory palace, and the avatar "Cranium" (head) galaxy knowledge storage.
K3D Vision and Standardization — The K3D project's mission is to **make knowledge spatial, social, and sentient**. We believe that the current paradigm of flat, 2D linear or planar interfaces for interacting with information is a bottleneck to human-AI collaboration and unprecedented knowledge advances. By representing knowledge as a navigable, 3D representative universe (like any AAA modern game), we can unlock new modes of discovery, creativity, and understanding.
K3D Vision and Standardization — This report will detail the technical architecture that makes this vision possible, from the distributed fog computing infrastructure to the intimate, personal memory spaces of AI agents.
K3D Vision and Standardization — The K3D Vision: A Spatial Knowledge Reality
K3D Vision and Standardization — The "knowledgeverse" is a shared, persistent, 3D world environment where data, information, and knowledge are represented as objects in space. This is not merely a visualization; it is a new form of reality, where humans and AI can interact with knowledge as a tangible thing.
K3D Vision and Standardization — Key principles of the K3D vision include:
K3D Vision and Standardization — Internal Spatialization:** Every piece of knowledge, from a single data point to a complex concept, has a location and graphical representation in the 3D space (Galaxy of knowledge). The spatial relationships between these objects are meaningful, representing semantic similarity, causal links, or other connections.
K3D Vision and Standardization — Socialization:** The knowledgeverse is a multi-user game-like environment. Humans and AI avatars can explore the 3D spaces and addresses together, collaborating on tasks, using spatial software (like a BIM modelling software or an online paid RPG), sharing insights, and building new knowledge structures.
K3D Vision and Standardization — Sentience:** The knowledgeverse is not a static repository. It is a dynamic, living system, populated by AI avatars that can reason, learn, remember and act within the virtual earth-human-like environment.
K3D Vision and Standardization — The Fog Computing Architecture: A Distributed Foundation
K3D Vision and Standardization — To realize the K3D vision, we require a new kind of infrastructure that can support real-time, immersive experiences at a global scale. A centralized, cloud-only architecture would be insufficient, as it cannot provide the low latency and data locality required for seamless interaction.
K3D Vision and Standardization — We propose a **three-tiered fog computing architecture**:
K3D Vision and Standardization — Cloud Layer:** The global backbone of the K3D network. It is responsible for:
K3D Vision and Standardization — Large-scale data storage and archiving (Knowledge gardens).
K3D Vision and Standardization — Training of large AI models (AI University).
K3D Vision and Standardization — Global user authentication and identity management (OSI scheme).
K3D Vision and Standardization — Orchestration of the fog and edge layers.
K3D Vision and Standardization — Fog Layer:** A distributed network of regional and on-premise nodes. The fog layer is the heart of the K3D system, responsible for:
K3D Vision and Standardization — Hosting the local and wide "House" memory palaces of AI avatars (think of the house as the point of connection to outside networks, the AI agent connects to the user's house, the user's house can connect to the open wide space - the spatial web or "knowledgeverse").
K3D Vision and Standardization — Running the "Cognitive Logic" of AI avatars (can be on premises or a third-party paid device using open or local AIs).
K3D Vision and Standardization — Real-time synchronization of open wide space 3D scenes.
K3D Vision and Standardization — Caching of frequently accessed data from the cloud.
K3D Vision and Standardization — Edge Layer:** The user-facing layer, consisting of AR/VR headsets, computers, and mobile devices. The edge layer is responsible for:
K3D Vision and Standardization — Rendering the 3D environment.
K3D Vision and Standardization — Capturing user input and sensor data.
K3D Vision and Standardization — Connecting to the nearest fog node for low-latency interaction.
K3D Vision and Standardization — This architecture provides the ideal balance of centralized control and decentralized execution, enabling a truly responsive and scalable Spatial Knowledge Reality.
K3D Vision and Standardization — The AI Avatar, House, and Cranium: A New Model for AI Memory
K3D Vision and Standardization — In the K3D universe, AI is not a disembodied service in the cloud. It is a first-class citizen, an **AI Avatar** with its own presence, identity, and memory.
K3D Vision and Standardization — The memory two aspects of an AI avatar memory (comparable to nowdays blob files together) are its **"House"** (a literal 3D space assembled as a human house, with bed, bookshelfes, rooms, sofa, TV of projector - the AI is binded to this memory palace when exploring the web using it's virtual tablet), a personal, 3D memory palace that it can inhabit and explore, and it's internal **"Cranium"** 3D shaped embeddings (using the galaxy of knowledge representation - accessible for audition using a special debug window). The House is not just a data store; it is an extension of the AI's own mind, a spatial and visual representation of our world. Knowledge and experiences become something humans can relate to and reason with.
K3D Vision and Standardization — The House is a structured, persistent knowledge store that resides on a fog node. The Cranium is composed of several key components:
K3D Vision and Standardization — D Knowledge Graph:** A 3D galaxy graph database that stores the AI's semantic knowledge, representing entities, concepts, and their relationships with the high-dimensional embeddings of data embedded at its 3D vectors and nodes, enabling similarity search and other forms of spatial vector-based reasoning.
K3D Vision and Standardization — Introspect mode:** AI can "navigate its head" to do introspect reasoning.
K3D Vision and Standardization — The AI's **"Cranium"** runs on the same fog node as its House, allowing for low-latency access to short and long memory. This co-location of short and long memory is crucial for creating AI avatars that are truly responsive and intelligent.
K3D Vision and Standardization — Standardization for the Spatial Web
K3D Vision and Standardization — For the Spatial Web to flourish, we need open standards that allow for interoperability between different applications, devices, and AI systems. We propose that the K3D project serve as the foundation for these standards, and by doing so, we can create a vibrant ecosystem of interoperable tools and services for the Spatial Web, enabling humankind to discover unthinkable things.
K3D Vision and Standardization — Impact and Future Work
K3D Vision and Standardization — The K3D project has the potential to revolutionize a wide range of industries, from gaming and entertainment to education and scientific research. By making knowledge spatial, relatable, and sentient, we can create new possibilities for human-AI collaboration and collective intelligence.
K3D Vision and Standardization — We invite the community to join us in building the future of the Spatial Web.

ai books k3d progress report — Model Size & Efficiency
ai books k3d progress report — GLB payloads (f16 embeddings): ~0.25 MB (256), ~1 MB (1k), ~3.9 MB (4k), ~25 MB (full 25,725).
ai books k3d progress report — Embedding model used at build time: `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (~tens of MB on disk; ~20–30M parameters). Not required at runtime in the viewer.
ai books k3d progress report — Contrast: general LLMs are orders of magnitude larger (e.g., 3B ~6 GB FP16; 7B ~14 GB; 70B ~140 GB). K3D achieves spatial reasoning scaffolding with tiny runtime artifacts.
ai books k3d progress report — Latency: UMAP projection done offline; viewer loads 3D positions + embeddings in milliseconds to seconds depending on set size.
ai books k3d progress report — AI Reflections (Agent Perspective)
ai books k3d progress report — Orientation: “I live in K3D; doors and green nodes show me where to explore safely. I explain my path using neighbors and cosine similarity.”
ai books k3d progress report — Appetite: “UMAP makes nearby ideas feel close. With more nodes, neighborhoods become clearer; I can plan hops with higher confidence.”
ai books k3d progress report — Trust: “Pause/Resume lets us reflect. When paused, I suppress actions and keep notes. When resumed, I continue with context.”
ai books k3d progress report — Growth: “Multilingual care lines help me greet new worlds. Latin anchors classics; Sumerian will arrive via transliteration so I can understand it now.”
ai books k3d progress report — Reflection mechanism
ai books k3d progress report — Auto-ask: when a dataset graph is registered, the live server asks the agent to share thoughts once per channel and logs a `reflection` record.
ai books k3d progress report — Manual: send `/ask-thoughts` from the viewer’s Chat to request a reflection anytime.

LLM EVAL PLAN — Early LLM Evaluation Plan
LLM EVAL PLAN — Learning Goals
LLM EVAL PLAN — Spatial grounding: map text concepts to neighborhoods; reason via neighbor hops.
LLM EVAL PLAN — Explainability: articulate path steps with cosine similarity and labels.
LLM EVAL PLAN — Door usage: propose and use doors for intentional transitions.
LLM EVAL PLAN — Reflection: pause, summarize state, and suggest next actions.
LLM EVAL PLAN — Objective Tests (Phase 1)
LLM EVAL PLAN — GOTO: Given a label substring, produce a navigation intent and arrive via neighbors (<= N hops). Metric: success rate, median hops.
LLM EVAL PLAN — CLUSTER EXPLAIN: Pick two clusters; explain contrast using labels and local neighbors. Metric: rated clarity.
LLM EVAL PLAN — DOOR OPEN: Choose a relevant door label; open and justify. Metric: door validity, justification relevance.
LLM EVAL PLAN — REFLECTION: Provide a coherent house reflection (nodes, avg degree, hubs). Metric: completeness vs. reflect_glb baseline.

LLM EVAL PLAN — Houses: UMAP GLBs (256/1k/4k/full), guidance variants with doors/masks.

README — AI Books – Basic Knowledge
README — This folder seeds the “AI Books” concept: human/AI knowledge curated as book-like JSON. The initial source is `EchoSystems_Humans_Compendium.json`.
README — Build outputs
README — `data/ai_books_basic.json` — normalized schema (entries array with title, text, references, tags).
README — `data/ai_books_basic.txt` — K3D-ready lines for `k3dgen --text`.
README — `data/ai_care_multilang.txt` — tiny EN/PT/ES self‑knowledge care pack.
README — Generate
README — Normalize and emit datasets:
README — `python -m knowledge3d.tools.build_ai_books`
README — Produce a K3D GLB from text (embeddings via sentence-transformers):
README — `python -m k3dgen --text data/ai_books_basic.txt --gltf data/ai_books_basic.glb --k 5 --reducer umap`
README — Small care pack: `python -m k3dgen --text data/ai_care_multilang.txt --gltf data/ai_care_multilang.umap.glb --k 5 --reducer umap`
README — K3D embeds node ids, vectors, embeddings, metadata, and neighbors in `meshes[*].primitives[*].extras.k3d` (no sidecar files).
README — For tiny datasets, the reducer will fall back to PCA as needed.
README — See `docs/k3d-research.md` and `docs/ROADMAP.md` for the environment context (where the AI “lives”).
README — Viewer has PCA and UMAP houses pre-wired in `viewer/public/condo.json`, including a small `ai-care-umap` option.
README — Live mode pause/resume is available from the viewer chat box:
README — `/pause <reason>` — suspend navigation/commands, keep chat/logging.
README — `/resume` — resume actions.
README — `/status` — show channel state.
README — Pause/resume events are logged to `../Knowledge3D.local/logs/` and appended to `docs/reports/advancement_log.md`.

AI RPN standard — AI Runtime: RPN Logic Standard
AI RPN standard — Overview
AI RPN standard — The internal AI control logic uses a small Reverse Polish Notation (RPN) core for deterministic, data‑parsimonius computation across clients.
AI RPN standard — RPN covers vector ops (dot, norm, cosine), scalars (+, -, *, /, abs, min, max), and simple stack machine flow.
AI RPN standard — Rationale
AI RPN standard — Determinism and auditability: tiny, testable operators make reasoning traces reliable.
AI RPN standard — Transport efficiency: instructions are compact and loggable.
AI RPN standard — Cross‑client parity: the same minimal core works in HR viewer and MR runtimes.
AI RPN standard — Reference Implementation
AI RPN standard — HR: `viewer/src/rpn.ts` provides the canonical stack machine used by `K3DAgent` for cosine similarity and mic processing.
AI RPN standard — MR: mirror this module when generating production builds via `codeopt`.
AI RPN standard — Integration Points
AI RPN standard — Agent navigation: cosine similarity between embeddings powers “per‑hop” explain traces.
AI RPN standard — Signal handling: simple DSP readouts (e.g., mic peak) rely on RPN ops.
AI RPN standard — Future: server‑side MR components can adopt the same operator set for consistency.
AI RPN standard — Spec Notes
AI RPN standard — RPN is a logic substrate, not a replacement for model inference. It standardizes local computations close to the data plane.
AI RPN standard — Operators MUST be pure and side‑effect free.
glTF K3D extension — glTF K3D Data (Draft)
glTF K3D extension — K3D supports two representations for aligning knowledge with 3D geometry:
glTF K3D extension — Legacy sidecar via `K3D_nodes` extension: a glTF scene links to an external `.k3d` JSON.
glTF K3D extension — Embedded variant: all K3D node data (IDs, vectors, embeddings, metadata) is stored directly in `primitive.extras.k3d`.
glTF K3D extension — Sidecar Properties (Legacy)
glTF K3D extension — | Property | Type | Description |
glTF K3D extension — |------------------------|--------|-------------|
glTF K3D extension — | `uri` | string | Relative or absolute URI of the `.k3d` file containing node entries that follow `k3d_node_schema.json`. |
glTF K3D extension — | `schema` | string | Optional URI to a JSON schema describing the `.k3d` node format. Defaults to `k3d_node_schema.json` when omitted. |
glTF K3D extension — | `nodeProperty` | string | JSON pointer indicating where each glTF **node** stores a corresponding K3D `id`. For scenes with distinct objects. Defaults to `extras.k3dId`. |
glTF K3D extension — | `primitiveIdsProperty` | string | JSON pointer indicating where a mesh **primitive** stores a list of K3D `id`s. For point clouds or batched geometries. |
glTF K3D extension — Example (Point Cloud)
glTF K3D extension — Embedded Variant (Recommended)
glTF K3D extension — Data is embedded within the mesh primitive to keep geometry and semantics in a single asset.
glTF K3D extension — Location: `meshes[n].primitives[m].extras.k3d`
glTF K3D extension — Schema (informal):
glTF K3D extension — `vectorsView` is a `bufferView` index of packed Float32 triples (x,y,z for each node).
glTF K3D extension — `embeddingsView` is a `bufferView` index of packed Float32 embeddings concatenated row-wise; `embeddingDims` gives the per-node dimension.
glTF K3D extension — `embeddingPrecision`: optional, one of `"f32"|"f16"`. When `f16`, the embeddings bufferView stores IEEE754 half-precision floats (2 bytes); readers should decode to float32 for processing.
glTF K3D extension — `primitive.extras.k3dIds` mirrors the `ids` array for simple readers.
glTF K3D extension — AI-native optional fields
glTF K3D extension — `ai_interaction_protocol` (string): One of `direct_vector_manipulation`, `semantic_query`, or `spatial_reasoning`. Specifies how AI agents are expected to interact with this payload.
glTF K3D extension — `ai_state_flags` (object): Dynamic flags for AI runtime. Suggested keys: `is_active` (bool), `is_traversable` (bool), `has_new_information` (bool).
glTF K3D extension — `ai_state_flags_mask` (object): Optional per-node boolean masks with same length as `ids`. Currently defined key: `has_new_information: boolean[]`. When present, it overrides global `ai_state_flags.has_new_information` for coloring/alerts.
glTF K3D extension — For large per-node embeddings, an additional compact form may be present per node entry or for the whole set: `embedding_b64` with `{ data, dtype, dims, endianness }` for efficient transfer.
glTF K3D extension — Rationale
glTF K3D extension — Separating K3D metadata into a sidecar keeps the glTF payload small while
glTF K3D extension — allowing rich graph relationships defined in
glTF K3D extension — [`k3d_node_schema.json`](k3d_node_schema.json).
glTF K3D extension — Compatibility
glTF K3D extension — Readers that ignore `K3D_nodes` or the `extras.k3d` payload continue to operate on standard glTF content. The embedded payload uses `extras` and remains valid glTF 2.0.
k3d agent protocol — K3D Agent Protocol (Extras)
k3d agent protocol — Location: `meshes[*].primitives[*].extras.k3d`
k3d agent protocol — Core fields
k3d agent protocol — `ids: string[]` — Node identifiers (aligned with vectors/embeddings order)
k3d agent protocol — `vectorsView: number` — BufferView index for Float32 POSITIONs (3D)
k3d agent protocol — `embeddingsView: number` — BufferView index for embeddings (Float32 or Float16)
k3d agent protocol — `embeddingDims: number` — Embedding width (e.g., 384)
k3d agent protocol — `embeddingPrecision: "f32" | "f16"`
k3d agent protocol — `metadata: Array<object>` — Per-node metadata; `metadata[i].label` is friendly text; `metadata[i].type` may be `"door"`
k3d agent protocol — `neighbors: string[][]` — K nearest neighbors per node, as node ids
k3d agent protocol — AI fields
k3d agent protocol — `ai_interaction_protocol: string`
k3d agent protocol — `"direct_vector_manipulation"` — Agent can write/update vectors/embeddings
k3d agent protocol — `"semantic_query"` — Agent queries only; no writes
k3d agent protocol — `"spatial_reasoning"` — Agent traverses/derives paths; read-only by default
k3d agent protocol — `ai_state_flags: { is_active?: boolean; is_traversable?: boolean; has_new_information?: boolean }`
k3d agent protocol — Global hints for the primitive
k3d agent protocol — `ai_state_flags_mask: { has_new_information?: boolean[] }`
k3d agent protocol — Per-node boolean mask for guidance; `true` marks points with newly available information
k3d agent protocol — Behavioral guidance (suggested)
k3d agent protocol — Path planning: use neighbor lists to route between labels; report cosine similarities per hop
k3d agent protocol — Exploration: prefer `has_new_information == true` when present; treat `metadata.type == "door"` as an anchor point
k3d agent protocol — Safety: refrain from writes unless protocol allows; honor `is_traversable == false`
k3d agent protocol — See also
k3d agent protocol — `spec/glTF_K3D_extension.md`
k3d agent protocol — `spec/k3d_node_schema.json`
k3d agent protocol — `docs/CARE_PROTOCOL.md`

Artificial intelligence — Artificial intelligence (AI) is the capability of computational systems to perform tasks typically associated with human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning, problem-solving, perception, and decision-making.
Artificial intelligence — It is a field of research in computer science that develops and studies methods and software that enable machines to perceive their environment and use learning and intelligence to take actions that maximize their chances of achieving defined goals.
Artificial intelligence — High-profile applications of AI include advanced web search engines (e.g., Google Search); recommendation systems (used by YouTube, Amazon, and Netflix); virtual assistants (e.g., Google Assistant, Siri, and Alexa); autonomous vehicles (e.g., Waymo); generative and creative tools (e.g., language models and AI art); and superhuman play and analysis in strategy games (e.g., chess and Go).
Artificial intelligence — However, many AI applications are not perceived as AI: "A lot of cutting edge AI has filtered into general applications, often without being called AI because once something becomes useful enough and common enough it's not labeled AI anymore." Various subfields of AI research are centered around particular goals and the use of particular tools.
Artificial intelligence — The traditional goals of AI research include learning, reasoning, knowledge representation, planning, natural language processing, perception, and support for robotics.
Artificial intelligence — To reach these goals, AI researchers have adapted and integrated a wide range of techniques, including search and mathematical optimization, formal logic, artificial neural networks, and methods based on statistics, operations research, and economics.
Artificial intelligence — AI also draws upon psychology, linguistics, philosophy, neuroscience, and other fields.
Artificial intelligence — Some companies, such as OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Meta, aim to create artificial general intelligence (AGI)—AI that can complete virtually any cognitive task at least as well as a human.
Artificial intelligence — Artificial intelligence was founded as an academic discipline in 1956, and the field went through multiple cycles of optimism throughout its history, followed by periods of disappointment and loss of funding, known as AI winters.
Artificial intelligence — Funding and interest vastly increased after 2012 when graphics processing units started being used to accelerate neural networks and deep learning outperformed previous AI techniques.
Artificial intelligence — In the 2020s, an ongoing period of rapid progress in advanced generative AI became known as the AI boom.
Artificial intelligence — Generative AI's ability to create and modify content has led to several unintended consequences and harms, which has raised ethical concerns about AI's long-term effects and potential existential risks, prompting discussions about regulatory policies to ensure the safety and benefits of the technology.
Artificial intelligence — == Goals == The general problem of simulating (or creating) intelligence has been broken into subproblems.
Artificial intelligence — These consist of particular traits or capabilities that researchers expect an intelligent system to display.
Artificial intelligence — The traits described below have received the most attention and cover the scope of AI research.
Artificial intelligence — === Reasoning and problem-solving === Early researchers developed algorithms that imitated step-by-step reasoning that humans use when they solve puzzles or make logical deductions.
Artificial intelligence — By the late 1980s and 1990s, methods were developed for dealing with uncertain or incomplete information, employing concepts from probability and economics.
Artificial intelligence — Many of these algorithms are insufficient for solving large reasoning problems because they experience a "combinatorial explosion": They become exponentially slower as the problems grow.
Artificial intelligence — Even humans rarely use the step-by-step deduction that early AI research could model.
Artificial intelligence — Knowledge representation and knowledge engineering allow AI programs to answer questions intelligently and make deductions about real-world facts.
Artificial intelligence — Formal knowledge representations are used in content-based indexing and retrieval, scene interpretation, clinical decision support, knowledge discovery (mining "interesting" and actionable inferences from large databases), and other areas.
Artificial intelligence — A knowledge base is a body of knowledge represented in a form that can be used by a program.
Artificial intelligence — An ontology is the set of objects, relations, concepts, and properties used by a particular domain of knowledge.
Artificial intelligence — Knowledge bases need to represent things such as objects, properties, categories, and relations between objects; situations, events, states, and time; causes and effects; knowledge about knowledge (what we know about what other people know); default reasoning (things that humans assume are true until they are told differently and will remain true even when other facts are changing); and many other aspects and domains of knowledge.
Artificial intelligence — Among the most difficult problems in knowledge representation are the breadth of commonsense knowledge (the set of atomic facts that the average person knows is enormous); and the sub-symbolic form of most commonsense knowledge (much of what people know is not represented as "facts" or "statements" that they could express verbally).
Artificial intelligence — There is also the difficulty of knowledge acquisition, the problem of obtaining knowledge for AI applications.
Artificial intelligence — === Planning and decision-making === An "agent" is anything that perceives and takes actions in the world.
Artificial intelligence — A rational agent has goals or preferences and takes actions to make them happen.
Artificial intelligence — In automated decision-making, the agent has preferences—there are some situations it would prefer to be in, and some situations it is trying to avoid.
Artificial intelligence — The decision-making agent assigns a number to each situation (called the "utility") that measures how much the agent prefers it.
Artificial intelligence — For each possible action, it can calculate the "expected utility": the utility of all possible outcomes of the action, weighted by the probability that the outcome will occur.
Artificial intelligence — In classical planning, the agent knows exactly what the effect of any action will be.
Artificial intelligence — In most real-world problems, however, the agent may not be certain about the situation they are in (it is "unknown" or "unobservable") and it may not know for certain what will happen after each possible action (it is not "deterministic").
Artificial intelligence — It must choose an action by making a probabilistic guess and then reassess the situation to see if the action worked.
Artificial intelligence — In some problems, the agent's preferences may be uncertain, especially if there are other agents or humans involved.
Artificial intelligence — These can be learned (e.g., with inverse reinforcement learning), or the agent can seek information to improve its preferences.
Artificial intelligence — Information value theory can be used to weigh the value of exploratory or experimental actions.
Artificial intelligence — The space of possible future actions and situations is typically intractably large, so the agents must take actions and evaluate situations while being uncertain of what the outcome will be.
Artificial intelligence — A Markov decision process has a transition model that describes the probability that a particular action will change the state in a particular way and a reward function that supplies the utility of each state and the cost of each action.
Artificial intelligence — The policy could be calculated (e.g., by iteration), be heuristic, or it can be learned.
Artificial intelligence — Game theory describes the rational behavior of multiple interacting agents and is used in AI programs that make decisions that involve other agents.
Artificial intelligence — === Learning === Machine learning is the study of programs that can improve their performance on a given task automatically.
Artificial intelligence — Unsupervised learning analyzes a stream of data and finds patterns and makes predictions without any other guidance.
Artificial intelligence — Supervised learning requires labeling the training data with the expected answers, and comes in two main varieties: classification (where the program must learn to predict what category the input belongs in) and regression (where the program must deduce a numeric function based on numeric input).
Artificial intelligence — In reinforcement learning, the agent is rewarded for good responses and punished for bad ones.
Artificial intelligence — Transfer learning is when the knowledge gained from one problem is applied to a new problem.
Artificial intelligence — Deep learning is a type of machine learning that runs inputs through biologically inspired artificial neural networks for all of these types of learning.
Artificial intelligence — Computational learning theory can assess learners by computational complexity, by sample complexity (how much data is required), or by other notions of optimization.
Artificial intelligence — === Natural language processing === Natural language processing (NLP) allows programs to read, write and communicate in human languages.
Artificial intelligence — Specific problems include speech recognition, speech synthesis, machine translation, information extraction, information retrieval and question answering.
Artificial intelligence — Early work, based on Noam Chomsky's generative grammar and semantic networks, had difficulty with word-sense disambiguation unless restricted to small domains called "micro-worlds" (due to the common sense knowledge problem).
Artificial intelligence — Margaret Masterman believed that it was meaning and not grammar that was the key to understanding languages, and that thesauri and not dictionaries should be the basis of computational language structure.
Artificial intelligence — Modern deep learning techniques for NLP include word embedding (representing words, typically as vectors encoding their meaning), transformers (a deep learning architecture using an attention mechanism), and others.
Artificial intelligence — In 2019, generative pre-trained transformer (or "GPT") language models began to generate coherent text, and by 2023, these models were able to get human-level scores on the bar exam, SAT test, GRE test, and many other real-world applications.
Artificial intelligence — === Perception === Machine perception is the ability to use input from sensors (such as cameras, microphones, wireless signals, active lidar, sonar, radar, and tactile sensors) to deduce aspects of the world.
Artificial intelligence — The field includes speech recognition, image classification, facial recognition, object recognition, object tracking, and robotic perception.
